title: Walkthrough of Your Vitable Partner Dashboard
body_markdown:
Most of what you need from an administrator is constant: Where does this group's enrollment stand? Which clients renew soon? What's the census format again?


Until now, most of those answers came from us over email or phone. Your Partner Dashboard moves them into your hands — here's everything that's behind it.


‍


## Home Page: Where Your Book Stands


Your landing screen answers two questions: how big is my book, and is anything on fire?


Two counters sit at the top: **active employers** and **total lives** . The active employers number counts the groups referred by or accessible to you that are currently active.


Underneath are three shortcuts: **Start a quote** , **View all employers** , and **Request a quote** if you'd rather have us build a personalized one and email it back.


Below that is an **announcements feed** : new carriers, new features, anything that changes how you sell.


‍


## Employers: Your Client List


This is the tab you'll live in. See every group you've placed here in one table.


Each row shows you:


- **Enrolled** : a live participation percentage and the raw count. This tells you instantly which groups need an enrollment push.
- **Active plans** : badges for every benefit the group has.
- **HRIS** : which payroll system is connected if any, and whether the connection is healthy.
- **Lifecycle** : status plus end date. This is a nudge for groups you should reach out to.


Search by name, EIN, or employer ID. **Filters** slice by plan type, HRIS status, HRIS provider, cancellation, and lifecycle stage.


Lifecycle is the filter worth learning. You can isolate groups that are **In OE** , **Renew soon** , **Active** , **Onboarding** , or **Cancelled** . Combine that with the enrollment column and you have a work queue: filter to *Renew soon* and sort out your upcoming calls.


**Export** creates a file from the filtered list. **Quote employer** starts a new quote without leaving the page.


## Inside the Client Detailed View


The header carries the practical details — FEIN, states, primary contact email — plus two counters: **active benefits today** and **total employees today (active and inactive)** .


Then a **Benefits** section, one card per plan, filterable to *Active & Upcoming* . Each card shows the monthly premium, enrollment count with a participation bar, the employee and employer contribution split, the open enrollment window, the coverage period, and a **plan documents** dropdown. If a client has ever asked "when does our OE close again?" mid-call, it's right here.


### The Employees tab


Every employee at the group, with contact details, **status** (active or terminated), **classification** (full time, part time), and **start date** . Search by name or email, **export the roster to CSV** , or **add an employee** directly — useful for a mid-year new hire when you don't want to wait on a census refresh.
*Note: If you have an HRIS system connected, you cannot use the Add an Employee button. The employer must add the new employee via their HRIS system, and the new employee will be brought over to Vitable on the next sync.*


### Payroll & Invoices tab


**Payroll deduction statements** , listed by pay period with the run date, employee count, and total — each downloadable as a CSV. The group's payroll frequency is labeled at the top. When a client's HR lead asks what to deduct this month, send them the file yourself.


**Invoices** , by period, with amount, paid status, and a **PDF download** . These are itemized, so you can see funding per employee rather than one lump figure.


### HRIS tab


Which payroll system is connected, and the timestamp and row count of the most recent sync. If a client says they added someone and you don't see them, check the last sync before you open a ticket.


## Members: Find Anyone, Fast


A searchable directory of every member across your book, with contact and address details. When you need to reach one employee, start here.


## Quoting: Building the Quote


Start with the basics — your email, your role, the company name — then pick the **quote year** . You can quote the current plan year or next, which matters right now with 1/1/2027 in play.


1. **Download the template.** A CSV with the exact columns required. No other format is accepted, which sounds rigid but saves a round trip.
2. **Add one row per person.** Employees, spouses and children each get their own row. Everyone in a family shares the same employee ID, and only the employee row carries income. Date of birth accepts YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY, zip must be five digits, relationship is Self / Spouse / Child, and yearly income is 0 for spouses and children.
3. **Upload it.** We validate the file before you continue, so a formatting problem surfaces immediately instead of after you've promised the client a turnaround.


Then set your starting parameters: contribution model, metal tier benchmark, Vitable Primary Care on or off, **your PEPM** (a slider up to $500, plus a fee discount field), and optionally the client's **current group health monthly cost** so the output becomes a savings comparison rather than a standalone price.


Hit submit and you land on the results page.
